content.user_title: Prepare Better Meetings with Notion Context
content.value_statement: Meeting preparation often scatters context across pages and leaves agendas incomplete. This skill gathers Notion context, selects a meeting format, and drafts tailored materials with cited research.
actual_capabilities: Collects meeting goals, attendees, timing, decisions, and prior materials through focused questions.
Searches and fetches relevant Notion pages, including notes, specifications, objectives, decisions, and action items.
Selects formats for status, decision, planning, retrospective, one-on-one, and brainstorming meetings.
Creates timeboxed agendas and pre-reads with source links, owners, expected outputs, risks, and preparation requests.
Adds cited market facts, benchmarks, risks, and best practices while separating facts from opinions.
Updates Notion pages and links follow-up tasks when authorized tools and destinations are available.
limitations: Requires a configured Notion MCP connection and successful user OAuth authentication.
Referenced templates and examples are not included in the scanned package, so their exact structures are unavailable.
External research can become outdated and requires human review before important decisions.
Page and task changes depend on the permissions granted to the connected Notion account.

use_cases.title: Plan Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Build a decision pre-read from specifications, prior discussions, open risks, and evaluation criteria.

use_cases.title: Prepare Executive Reviews
use_cases.description: Summarize progress, blockers, benchmarks, and required decisions in a concise, timeboxed review.

use_cases.title: Structure Team Sessions
use_cases.description: Create focused planning, retrospective, one-on-one, or brainstorming agendas with owners and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Agenda
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a {meeting type} for {date}. Ask me for missing goals, attendees, duration, decisions, and source pages before drafting the agenda.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start meeting preparation when only basic details are available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Contextual Agenda
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Notion for context about {project}. Summarize relevant decisions, risks, open actions, and source links, then draft a timeboxed agenda for {attendees}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use existing workspace context to prepare a project meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Decision Pre-Read
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a decision pre-read for {decision}. Compare {options} against {criteria}, identify evidence gaps, assign discussion owners, and cite relevant Notion sources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare stakeholders to evaluate options and reach a documented decision.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Executive Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an executive review for {initiative} using Notion history and current research. Separate facts from opinions, flag conflicting evidence, and propose decision checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine internal history and external evidence for a high-stakes review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a 45-minute sprint planning session for the product and engineering leads.
output_examples.output: Goal: commit to a realistic sprint scope. Agenda: context review, capacity check, priority discussion, dependency review, and commitment. Each section includes an owner and timebox.

output_examples.input: Create a pre-read for choosing between two customer support platforms.
output_examples.output: The pre-read states the decision, evaluation criteria, available evidence, unresolved questions, risks, and recommendation options. It links each internal claim to its Notion source.

output_examples.input: Prepare a one-on-one agenda using recent notes and open actions.
output_examples.output: The agenda covers progress, blockers, feedback, development goals, and prior commitments. It closes with named actions and target dates.

best_practices: Confirm the meeting objective, required decisions, attendees, and duration before searching or drafting.
Review the Notion search scope and page destination before reading or writing sensitive workspace content.
Verify external claims, retain source links, and label uncertain conclusions before sharing materials.
anti_patterns: Do not create or update pages before confirming the destination and granted permissions.
Do not present uncited external research or assumptions as established facts.
Do not overload the agenda with topics that lack owners, timeboxes, or expected outputs.

faq.question: Does this skill require Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. Searching, fetching, creating, and updating workspace content requires a configured Notion MCP connection.

faq.question: Can it connect to Notion automatically?
faq.answer: No. The user must add the Notion MCP endpoint, enable remote MCP support, complete OAuth, and restart Codex.

faq.question: Which meeting formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow covers status, decision, planning, retrospective, one-on-one, and brainstorming meetings.

faq.question: Can it edit existing meeting pages?
faq.answer: Yes, when the connected Notion account has access and the user authorizes the target page.

faq.question: How does it handle research?
faq.answer: It adds concise external context, keeps claims linked to sources, and separates factual evidence from opinion.

faq.question: Are templates included with this package?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package references template and example directories, but only the main skill instructions are present.
